title: Beyond Classification Accuracy: A Stability-Driven and Explainable Multi-Stage Radiomics Framework for Breast Ultrasound Image Classification
content: Objective: The aim of this study is to reduce high-dimensional radiomic features extracted from breast ultrasound images into compact and stable subsets using a multi-stage feature selection process, and to evaluate the effectiveness of these features in classifying benign and malignant breast lesions through various machine learning algorithms. Methods: A total of 647 breast ultrasound images comprising 437 benign and 210 malignant cases obtained from the Breast Ultrasound Images (BUSI) dataset were used in this study. A total of 753 radiomic features were extracted using PyRadiomics, including first-order statistical, shape, and texture features, as well as features derived from wavelet and Laplacian of Gaussian transforms. To reduce feature dimensionality, a multi-stage feature selection approach was employed, consisting of variance filtering, correlation analysis, Mutual Information, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). Compact radiomic feature sets comprising five and ten features—were evaluated using nine machine learning algorithms through three-, five-, and ten-fold stratified cross-validation. Final model performance was assessed using an 80% development and 20% hold-out test split. Classification performance was evaluated through bootstrap confidence intervals, DeLong and McNemar tests, as well as calibration and decision curve analyses. Feature selection stability and model explainability were investigated using selection frequency, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), and permutation importance analyses. Results: As a result of a multi-stage feature selection process, compact candidate sets consisting of five and ten features were constructed. SVM and MLP models stood out due to their high classification performance. Explainability analyses, classification performance, and feature selection stability have provided significant opportunities for the multidimensional assessment of the diagnostic potential of compact radiomic feature sets.Conclusions: This study contributes to a comprehensive analysis of compact radiomics-based classification approaches by integrating explainability analyses, feature selection stability, statistical comparisons, and thorough model validation. For future research, validation using multi-center and independent datasets may be required to demonstrate clinical generalizability.
